# PXBOT NQ Console — Data Integrity Report

**Generated:** 2026-08-02, from a full run of `data/download.js` against the live, connected
TradeLocker account.
**Identity:** provider=`tradelocker`, broker=`GenFX`, symbol=`NAS100`, instrumentId=`8530`,
routeId=`541038`.
**Source of truth:** `data/logs/DATA_INTEGRITY_REPORT.json` (machine-readable, regenerated by
`node -r ./scripts/load_env.js data/download.js` on every run — gitignored as regenerable output,
not source). This file is the human-readable summary of that run.

## Reproduction

```
cp .env.example .env        # fill in real TradeLocker email/password/server
node -r ./scripts/load_env.js data/download.js                     # full download, all resolutions
node -r ./scripts/load_env.js data/download.js --resolutions=1m    # single resolution
node -r ./scripts/load_env.js data/download.js --force             # re-probe past a resolution already marked exhausted
```

## What "0 duplicates / 0 malformed / 0 out-of-order" actually means

- **Duplicates**: structurally prevented by the store's primary key
  `(provider, broker, account_id, symbol, instrument_id, route_id, resolution, time)` — an upsert
  overwrites rather than duplicates. The integrity scan re-checks this independently over the
  actual stored rows (not just trusting the schema) and found none.
- **Malformed**: every bar is checked for `open/high/low/close > 0` and internal OHLC consistency
  (`high >= low`, `high >= open/close`, `low <= open/close`) before it's even written to the store
  (`data/downloader.js`'s `validateBars`) — none were rejected in this run, i.e. TradeLocker's raw
  responses were clean for this instrument.
- **Out-of-order**: bars are required to be strictly increasing in time within a batch and across
  upserts; none were found.

## Gaps — the honest picture

A gap is only counted as "unexplained" if it exceeds both a resolution-scaled tolerance
(3× the expected bar spacing) **and** a 30-hour flat floor (covering ordinary daily halts), and
does **not** fall across a Friday-evening-to-Sunday-evening window (NAS100/NQ's real ~24×5
Globex-hours trading schedule, matching the same weekend heuristic `server.js` already uses).

All residual "unexplained" gaps were manually inspected against their dates:

- 1D: 21 gaps — Christmas/New Year, Good Friday/Easter, July 4th, Thanksgiving, in every year
  2015–2025, plus a 17-day gap right at 2015-04-13 (the very first stored bar — likely the true
  edge of the broker's historical archive rather than a mid-series defect; flagged, not asserted).
- 4H/1H/30m/15m: 9-10 gaps each, same holiday pattern, 2024-2026.
- 5m/1m: 4 gaps each, same holiday pattern within the shorter Nov-2025–Jul-2026 window.

No exchange holiday calendar is wired in yet, so these are flagged rather than silently
suppressed — that is deliberate: a false "clean" report would be worse than a few holiday entries
a human can glance at and dismiss in seconds, per this project's rule against hiding or
auto-explaining away anomalies.

## The one finding that changes downstream planning

Retention depth is **not uniform by resolution**: 15m and coarser share one retention floor
(2024-01-01, ~2.6 years), while 5m and 1m share a much shorter one (2025-11-06, ~267 days). This
was confirmed by four independent resolutions landing on the identical 2024-01-01 boundary and two
independent resolutions landing on the identical 2025-11-06 boundary — not a single ambiguous
result, but agreement across independently-paginated series, which is the strongest evidence this
downloader can produce that these are real broker-side retention limits, not a bug in the
pagination logic itself.

**Consequence:** genuine 1-minute-execution backtesting (the standard the mission requires for the
primary execution engine) is currently bounded to ~267 days of real data. Coarser structural
analysis (session/range definitions, regime context) can draw on ~2.6 years. Long-horizon
seasonality/regime context can draw on the full ~11.3-year daily series. This is carried forward
into `CURRENT_STRATEGY_BASELINE.md` and the walk-forward/holdout design rather than papered over.
The store's incremental top-up (re-running the downloader) means the 1-minute window grows by one
real day for every day the account stays connected — this is a starting point, not a ceiling.
